meta.description: Common kanji radicals (部首), grouped by theme. Each entry lists the radical, its Japanese name, and a few kanji it appears in.

words.note: The simplest radical, a single horizontal stroke. It appears in kanji like 天 (heaven) and 元 (origin) as the top stroke.
Two stacked horizontal strokes. Commonly seen in 元 and 示, and as part of compound numbers.
Three horizontal strokes. It hides inside kanji like 春 (spring), whose top part is a variant of 三.
A cross of two strokes. It appears in 計 (count) and 古 (old).
Two strokes opening downward. Seen in 公 (public) and 分 (part), where the 'two-part' sense splits things apart.
The left-side water radical. Almost every kanji related to water or liquids uses it: 海 (sea), 泳 (swim), 湯 (hot water).
The standalone water character. 氷 (ice) is water with an extra stroke on the left.
Three flowing strokes. It appears on the right side of 順 (order) and 訓 (instruction).
The standalone person radical. In 休 (rest) a person 亻 leans against a tree 木 — the picture of resting.
The compressed person radical on the left. Words about people or their actions use it: 休 (rest), 体 (body), 住 (live).
A tree — the vertical trunk with two branches. One tree is 木, two are 林 (grove), three are 森 (forest).
The grass/plant crown on top of a character. Found in 花 (flower), 茶 (tea), and 草 (grass).
A square representing an open mouth. It stacks to form 品 (goods) and appears in 問 (ask).
Speech — lines coming out of a mouth. Words about speaking or words themselves carry it: 話 (talk), 語 (language).
The standalone hand. 持 (hold) combines it with the temple radical.
The compressed hand on the left, used in almost every hand-action verb: 打 (hit), 持 (hold), 指 (point).
The standalone heart. In 思 (think) it sits under a field 田 — thoughts growing from the heart/mind.
The vertical heart on the left. Emotions and states of mind use it: 情 (feeling), 忙 (busy), 快 (pleasant).
The sun. It brightens 明 (bright, with 月) and measures 時 (time).
The moon. Paired with 日 it forms 明 (bright); it also counts months in 期 (period).
The standalone fire, a person 人 with sparks flying. 燃 (burn) and 炭 (charcoal) carry it.
Four flames at the bottom of a character, the compressed fire radical. Seen in 煮 (boil), 熱 (heat), and 然 (so).
Earth as ground. Land words use it: 地 (ground), 場 (place), 城 (castle).
Three peaks. Found in 岩 (rock) and 峰 (peak).
A rock under a cliff. 研 (polish, study) — polishing on a stone — and 確 (certain) carry it.
A divided rice paddy. It sits inside 男 (man, 'field + strength') and 思 (think).
Gold in the earth, its ore glinting. Money is お金, and metal characters like 銀 (silver) take it as their base.
The compressed metal radical on the left. Nearly every metal name uses it: 銀 (silver), 鉄 (iron), 銅 (copper).
A kneeling woman. It appears in 好 (like — a woman with a child) and 姉 (older sister).
A swaddled baby. 学 (study) shows a child 子 under a canopy of learning.
An eye turned sideways. 見 (see) is an eye 目 on legs 儿; 眠 (sleep) closes the eye.
Clouds with raindrops. Weather kanji fall from it: 雪 (snow) and 雲 (cloud).
A roof. Home words shelter under it: 家 (house), 宿 (lodging), 安 (peace).
A road and a foot. Movement words walk with it: 道 (road), 進 (advance), 近 (near).
A skein of thread. Fiber and connection words use it: 線 (line), 紙 (paper), 約 (promise, binding).
A flat dish or plate. 血 (blood) is a drop into the dish; 盛 (heap) serves up food on it.
A sword. Cutting words carry it: 切 (cut), 分 (divide, a blade splitting), 初 (first — first cut of cloth).
